note:
Thirty-five measured regions resolve to 19 figure rows, 1 table row and 15 exclusions, with nothing unaccounted. The exclusions split four ways: eight pasted display-mathematics regions (the Fresnel pair on p5, equations (5)-(6) on p6, (9)-(13) on p8, (14)-(15) on p9, (16)-(19) on p11, (22)-(23) on p12, the attenuation factor and equation (25) on p13), one raster duplicate of the Fresnel pair, one running-header and heading rule band on p5, one caption band on p8 and three raster copies of vector figure frames on pp18-19.

What this paper adds to the lane. (1) It is the first document in the batch whose captions record a full-width colon - 'Figure 6：The relationship between Lcal or Ltur and f' - which no numbering vocabulary covers, so the numbering field takes the bare 'Figure N' form and this note carries the punctuation. (2) It prints one plot template four times: the hop-budget frame with a dashed 150 dB threshold and an n = 1..k key appears as Figure 10 (calm sea, n = 1..8), Figure 12 left (smooth terrain, n = 1..8), Figure 12 right (rugged, n = 1..5) and Figure 13 (shipboard, n = 1..5), and only the caption and the key change. (3) It repeats a second template twice: Figure 7 and Figure 11 are the same received-power curve against frequency, one for sea states and one for terrains, and they share the misspelt axis 'frequence / (Hz)' in a paper whose band is 3-30 MHz. (4) Both of the paper's schematic pair - Figures 1 and 2 - are drawn in the same vocabulary (Earth arc, dashed ionosphere arcs, ray fan, R/Z/θ labels) and neither is cited from the body for Figure 2. (5) The paper is the lane's clearest case of a caption hiding a unit error that the artwork repeats: no caption prints a unit, one axis prints Hz for MHz, and the one grid omits the unit of both σ columns.

Defects worth recording. Figure 1's ionospheric arcs are unlabelled; Figure 2's label chain reuses θ for two different quantities; Figure 3 has no colourbar and no panel letters, so which panel belongs to which wind speed is only inferable from a rotated z label; Figure 4 draws no normal vectors in a section about normal-vector distributions; Figure 5's two panels differ by two orders of magnitude with nothing but tick labels to say so; Figure 7's key reads 'clam oceean'; Figure 10's y title reads 'attennation' and its x10^4 multiplier contradicts the '(km)' unit in its caption; Figure 11's key reads 'rugid terrain'; Figure 12's right panel raises the y ceiling 40 dB without saying so; Figure 13's five arcs do not meet, leaving two thirds of the frame empty; Figure 14's tick values (2767, 5786) are transposed against the prose's own ranges (2676, 5768) and no key explains its red spans; Figure 15's key uses w where the glossary defines U19.5; Figure 16's caption stutters and its four curves overlap so completely that the exhibit proves only that the perturbation is invisible; and Table 1 gives no unit for σ. Every page also carries a red Chinese shop-watermark band in the running header.

Coverage note for the lane. The abbreviation glossary at the top of p5 - a fifteen-row, two-column 'Abbreviation / Full Name' table - is a real table and is not in the layout at all: the detector boxed the rule band above it (p5 r1) and nothing else. It is therefore not recordable as a table row without inventing a bbox. The same page shows why: the detector's raster/vector pair on p5 is one pasted equation block measured twice, while the well-ruled native table beside it is not measured at all - the region pass follows images, not tables.

Section grammar. Section 3 is where everything is drawn, in the order the model is built: geometry (1, 2), the wave simulation (3), the microplane construction (4), the reflection loss (5-7), the path budget (8), the ionosphere (9), the hop count (10), the terrain comparison (Table 1, 11, 12), the shipboard correction (13, 14), and then section 4 spends its three rows asking whether the answer moves when the wind, εr or σ move. Each modelling step gets exactly one exhibit, and the only two exhibits nobody cites (Figures 2 and 9) are the two the authors did not draw themselves.
rules: Numbering is one colon grammar across the whole paper - 18 of the 19 figure rows print 'Figure N:' and the single grid prints 'Table N:' - with exactly one exception, Figure 6, which is the batch's only caption printed with a full-width colon 'Figure 6：' [caption.numbering].

Caption side is decided by exhibit kind and inverted between the two kinds: all 19 figure rows print their caption BELOW the artwork and the one table row prints ABOVE its grid, so the paper's single grid is also its single above-caption [caption.position].

Three captions carry a second printed line that the artwork cannot say itself - 'n: number of hops, f = 3MHz, reflected by calm oceans' and its two variants on Figures 10, 12 and 13 - which makes the caption the only place the parameter setting of a hop-budget plot is written down [caption.sentences].

Captions are short and flat: the 19 figure captions run 7 to 27 words with a median of 15, the three shortest are bare noun phrases ('Propagation path of sky wave', 'the range of effective signal') and the three longest are the hop-budget titles that carry a second subtitle line [caption.words].

Captions name symbols rather than media - 11 of the 19 name between one and four of Lbf, Lcal, Ltur, Lt, n, f, εr and σ - and 10 of the 19 pin a parameter setting inside the caption itself (wind speed on Figures 3 and 15, f = 3MHz on Figures 5, 6, 10, 12 and 13, the f = 3/12/21/30MHz grid on Figure 8), which is the only reason the plots can be re-derived [caption.variable_count].

Two captions are defective at the level of the noun: Figure 16 stutters - 'the change of the change of Ltur' - and Figure 5 says 'tough surface' where the section heading and the symbol both say turbulent [caption.concludes].
No caption concludes, and no caption prints a unit for its own axis, although one axis title inside the artwork carries a unit that contradicts the caption's [caption.units].

The paper draws with one engine and one hand: 14 of the 19 figure rows are MATLAB line plots (single frame, joined traces, no markers, no colourbar, no printed values), 4 are hand-drawn schematics with no axes at all, and 1 is the single four-panel surface plot [geometry.family].

Three-dimensional drawing happens exactly once: Figure 3's four surf panels in a 2x2 grid, shaded with mesh lines, each panel on its own z scale, and with no colourbar - so the height field that the section is about cannot be read numerically from the print [geometry.three_d].

Keys are never outside the frame: 11 rows key inside (upper right for the single-frame sweeps, lower right for the hop-budget template, inside-right for the eight-entry case) and the other 8 rows carry no key at all, four because they are schematics and four because Figure 5 and Figure 9 title their panels from inside the axes instead [geometry.legend].

Panel grammar is thin and stated nowhere: Figure 3 is one measured region holding four panels, Figures 5 and 12 are each split into two measured regions by the export gutter, and Figure 9 borrows a shared altitude axis across its pair; no (a)/(b) letters exist, and the only panel labelling in the paper is the words '(left)' and '(right)' inside Figure 12's caption [geometry.panel_count].

Shared axes are used twice and both times to save a scale rather than to invite comparison: Figure 9 shares the altitude strip and Figure 5 deliberately does not share its y, so the two panels of Figure 5 differ by two orders of magnitude while sitting side by side [geometry.shared_axes].

The last three figures are image exports rather than live vector plots: each is measured twice, once as its vector frame and once as the raster inside it, so the record keeps one row per figure and excludes the copy [geometry.printed_numbers].

The single grid is booktabs with merged header spans and nothing else: no zebra, no slanting corner, no vertical rules, no note row, no continuation, and no unit anywhere in the σ columns [table.rule_style].

Header depth is two rows because two spanners are needed - 'Geology' across both rows and εr and σ each across a Range/Average pair - and the merged cells are the only structural device the grid uses [table.merged_cells].

Shading never appears: no grid in this paper has zebra banding, and the only ruled non-grid surface in the paper is the abbreviation glossary on p5, which the detector does not box as a region [table.zebra].

Announcement is same-page for 14 rows and one page early for 4 - Figure 3 is foreshadowed in the calm-ocean section and Figures 13, 14 and 15 are named on the page before they print - so section 3.4.2 is the only place where the prose outruns the artwork [mention.lead_pages].

Citation vocabulary is a four-phrase rotation: 'figure N shows', 'As shown in the figure N', 'From figure N we can find' and 'The result was displayed in figure N', with no exhibit analysed in more than three sentences anywhere in the paper [mention.style].

Two exhibits are never cited in the body at all - Figure 2 and Figure 9 - and both are borrowed or purely explanatory: Figure 2 is a geometry schematic and Figure 9 is a textbook plate whose caption carries the reference [mention.count].

Placement tracks the derivation down the page: 9 of the 20 rows sit in the middle band, 8 in the top third and 3 at the foot, and all three foot cases are hop-budget or terrain plots that end a section [place.page_zone].

Exhibit density follows the model: the introduction carries 1 row, the modelling sections 3.1-3.4 carry 16, the sensitivity section carries 3, and the two closing pages carry none - no figure, no table, no pasted equation in the strengths, weakness, note or reference pages [place.section_kind].

Every measured box outside the exhibit rows is pasted display mathematics (8 boxes), a copy of a box the detector already holds (4: three raster interiors of vector figure frames and one raster copy of the Fresnel pair), a caption band (1), a running-header rule band (1) or a fragment of a frame (1) [place.area_frac].
